turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I treated the strongest signals in the training set as coming from whole-stack motifs, not isolated materials. The best candidates are those combining:

- **Fullerene ETL + strong cathode buffer**: PCBM/C60 with BCP, Bphen, TPBi/TmPyPB-like N-rich blockers suppresses interfacial recombination and improves electron selectivity.
- **High-quality HTLs**: PTAA and well-tuned NiO-based contacts outperform simple PEDOT:PSS unless PEDOT:PSS is paired with an excellent cathode buffer.
- **Benign back contacts**: Cu/Ag/Al can all work, but Cu with PTAA/C60/BCP appears especially strong in the training set.
- **Interface passivation / plasmonic or dipole modifiers**: Au-np/NiO and non-fullerene acceptor interlayers are associated with the highest measured recipes.

Most likely top candidates:

1. **c040** — PCBM-60 | TPBi / PEDOT:PSS / Al is the closest physics analogue to the top training motif PCBM-60 | TmPyPB / PEDOT:PSS, using an N-rich cathode buffer that should passivate and improve electron extraction.
2. **c030** — IDTT2FPDI | PCBM-60 | Bphen with PTAA | PMMA / Al closely matches a very high-performing Bphen/PTAA/PMMA stack, with an additional acceptor interlayer likely improving extraction.
3. **c038** — PEI + Au-np | NiO-c resembles the very strong Au-np/NiO-c training motif; Au nanoparticles and NiO can improve hole extraction and reduce interface losses.
4. **c088** — C60 | BCP / PTAA / Cu matches the high-performing C60/BCP/PTAA/Cu family; Cu contact and PTAA selectivity are favorable.
5. **c044** — PCBM-60 | BCP / PTAA / Cu is another close member of the same high-efficiency PTAA/Cu family, though slightly less favorable than the C60 analogue.

Final: c040, c030, c038, c088, c044
